lens: CHEAT DETECTOR (hardcoding, oracle, weld, teleport, scope, planner invariance)

findings.title: D3 writes grasp_body as a body id, but TAMPURA's reward unifies holding with is-target over STORE SYMBOLS; as specified the O arm can never score 1.0 and the G6 fault tests pass vacuously
findings.problem: Their abstract() emits holding(self.grasp_body) and is-target(o) for o in self.world.objects, and the belief's world is sim_world whose .objects were replaced by store symbols at initialize (env.py:849-851). Their own pick_execute_fn sets obs.grasp_body = obj, the store symbol from action.args (env.py:362, 394). The reward is Exists ?o: is-target(?o) and holding(?o). D3 says grasp_body = 'the contacted body's id (never the target's name)': holding(<int>) never unifies with is-target('o_ph_k'), so every O episode scores 0 regardless of what the arm did. The plan's G6 unit tests (force no_path, force lift failure, assert reward 0) would all pass on this broken adapter because reward is always 0, so the gate would certify the defect. The implementation-time 'fix' is exactly the kind of ad hoc belief write the contract polices.
findings.evidence: env.py:306-315 (abstract: holding(grasp_body), is-target over self.world.objects), env.py:849-851 (sim_world.objects = store.add_typed(o,'physical')), env.py:362,394 (grasp_body = obj symbol), env.py:70-73 (obs_from_camera_image resolves body -> symbol via store.get(obj_sym) == body); plan line: 'grasp_body = the contacted body's id (never the target's name)'
findings.required_change: D3: grasp_body = the store symbol s in env.sim_world.objects with store.get(s) == the contacted body id, resolved through THEIR AliasStore exactly as obs_from_camera_image does (same identity map, declared); grasp = a sentinel value added through store.add_typed(<bridge grasp record>, 'grasp') so holding is emitted (env.py:309) and verify/pickling stay valid. G6 gains a POSITIVE control: an adapter observation built from a readback where the contacted body's category is 'dice' and conf == DEFAULT_ARM_POS must yield reward 1.0, and the same readback with a cup body must yield 0.0; the fault tests are only meaningful after the positive control passes.

findings.title: D4 makes the wrist camera at q_home the fixed eye, but the main pipeline renders outside sense actions from a cached fixed camera; in their world that is a disembodied sensor
findings.plan_location: D4, M1, B2 (env_adapter camera params 'from the camera_frame link state at q_home')
findings.problem: Every render goes through env.detect_objects(), whose view matrix is built from the env's fixed camera_position/camera_target attributes (boxel_env.py:1620-1624, 1723-1738). The pipeline renders at many points other than sense: the census (execution.py:343), refresh_object_aabbs after pick and place (execution.py:821-824, 1799, 1954, 2102, 2602, 2753, 3028, 3093), F20 registration. With the camera defined once from the camera_frame link at q_home, every one of those renders while the arm is mid-manipulation is taken from a pose the physical wrist camera does not occupy: a teleported sensor, an oracle in disguise. It also means M1's at_config precondition is enforced only symbolically; a sense executed after a move that did not physically reach q_home would still render from the home viewpoint.
findings.evidence: boxel_env.py:1620-1624 (_view_and_projection_matrices from self.camera_position/self.camera_target), boxel_env.py:1723-1741 (detect_objects uses them), execution.py:343, 821-824, 1799, 1954, 2102, 2602, 2753, 3028, 3093 (renders outside sense); plan line: 'camera params from the camera_frame link state at q_home'
findings.required_change: env_adapter computes the view matrix from the LIVE camera_frame link state at every render and logs it; new gate (G20): per render, view matrix == pose of camera_frame at render time, and for every sense render max joint error to q_home below the executor's own endpoint tolerance, otherwise the sense is an executor failure, not an observation. Pre-register in a BF# which of the two honest options applies to non-sense renders: (a) suppress refresh_object_aabbs/census renders while the arm is away from q_home (a behaviour change for the bridge path, gated by a switch that our scenes leave off and A/B as in B3), or (b) accept moving-camera refreshes as a declared model tweak M1b with its own BEFORE/AFTER/CLAIM EFFECT lines. Option (a) is the one consistent with 'the camera is fixed'.

findings.title: G8 contradicts the main pipeline it claims to preserve: the hidden target's id is in streams.object_body_ids and in the sense classifier from step 0 today; the identity map must be declared and bounded, not denied
findings.plan_location: G8, D1 ('as today'), B2 (objects table), G2
findings.problem: main() builds object_body_ids over EVERY env.objects entry, hidden target included (test_full_pipeline.py:890-893), and handle_sense_action reads env.objects[target_name].object_id on every sense and hands it to sense_shadow_from_render as the target's seg id (execution.py:2474, 2513-2517), which execution.py:88-89 calls 'the accepted sim-grade identity map standing in for a recognition model'. G8 as written ('set(streams.object_body_ids) == set(registry OBJECT boxel names) ... the target's id present before its first appearance fails') is therefore red on the main pipeline on day one. It can only go green by building a bridge-specific object table (so D1's 'our whole pipeline as today' is false) or by quietly weakening the gate; both are the drift the plan is meant to prevent. Meanwhile the real leak channel is untouched: ObjectInfo.position is filled with TRUE poses by update_object_positions (boxel_env.py:1856-1869), which main() calls during the episode (test_full_pipeline.py:564, 1734, 1845, 1906, 2085, 2153), and G2's grep would see only the one call site in boxel_env.py.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:890-893; execution.py:2474, 2513-2517, 88-89; boxel_env.py:1856-1869; test_full_pipeline.py:1734, 1845, 1906, 2085, 2153; streams.py:530-549 (boxel_fits uses NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS, the previous getAABB leak already closed); boxel_env.py:751-753 (plan twin parks bodies with no boxel)
findings.required_change: Re-specify G8 as the identity-map boundary: (a) env_adapter.objects is the seg-id -> name/category map built from their world.objects/world.categories (the same map TAMPURA applies at env.py:70-73) and carries no position/orientation/AABB for any body without an OBJECT boxel; update_object_positions is a no-op on the adapter and its main() call sites are gated by the B3 settings object; (b) runtime hook: p.getAABB, p.getBasePositionAndOrientation, p.getClosestPoints and p.getContactPoints raise when called with the body id of a name that has no OBJECT boxel, except inside sync_to_plan_client's static branch, the scoring adapter and world_integrity_check; (c) assert after every sync that the plan-twin pose of every boxel-less body equals _PLAN_CLIENT_PARK; (d) the record and the paper state the identity map as the shared perception assumption of both systems.

findings.title: G16 and B3(d) cannot both hold: main() runs the Phase-4 oracle split unconditionally and picks the holding target from it with random.choice
findings.problem: main() calls env.oracle_detect_objects() unconditionally at test_full_pipeline.py:692 (and at :576 when n_hidden_targets > 0), computes hidden_targets_set from it, and for the holding goal sets target_name = random.choice(hidden_targets_ordered) from that oracle split (test_full_pipeline.py:728-733). B3(d) promises an injected env plus settings object with 'no behaviour change', and G16 promises that oracle_detect_objects and the Phase-4 split are absent from the bridge's episode path with a hook counter reading 0. Without a stated mechanism the implementer either gives the adapter an oracle_detect_objects (G16 red) or edits main() in a way that changes our own scenes (the random.choice at :732 consumes the global RNG; removing it on our scenes shifts every later draw).
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:576, 692-693, 728-733 (target_name = random.choice over the oracle hidden split), 802-805; boxel_env.py:1792-1854 (oracle_detect_objects reads true poses and AABBs of every body)
findings.required_change: B3(d) names the settings fields explicitly: target_name (resolved by category from the task spec on the bridge) and oracle_phases (default True). With oracle_phases False, main() skips the :576 check and all of Phase 4, takes target_name from settings, and raises if the env exposes oracle_detect_objects at all. With True (our scenes) the code path, including the random.choice, stays byte-identical, which the B3 A/B must show through identical target choices per seed. G16's runtime counter hooks oracle_detect_objects AND update_object_positions.

findings.title: G11 would not have caught the archived direct solve() pattern, and 'the very list solve() returned' is false even for the main pipeline
findings.problem: The archived Phase 3-C generation built a one-cup init by hand and called pddlstream's solve() directly (boxel_policy.py:68-105); it never instantiated PDDLStreamPlanner, so 'type(planner).plan is PDDLStreamPlanner.plan' either passes vacuously or does not apply. Separately, PDDLStreamPlanner.plan converts solve()'s plan into a NEW list of tuples before returning (pddlstream_planner.py:1202-1209), so an id-equality test against solve()'s list can never pass; an implementer will relax it, and a relaxed G11 no longer excludes a _convert_plan between planner and dispatcher.
findings.evidence: archive/tampura_bridge_v1/boxel_policy.py:68-105 (plan_solve: hand-built init, solve(problem, unit_costs=True)); archive/tampura_bridge_v1/boxel_policy.py:255-262 (_plan_attempt with known_empty_shadows=all_shadows); pddlstream_planner.py:1131-1154, 1202-1209
findings.required_change: G11 = (i) grep: no 'pddlstream' import anywhere in tampura_bridge/ or in any episode-path module other than pddlstream_planner.py and streams.py; (ii) runtime hook on pddlstream.algorithms.meta.solve asserting the calling frame is PDDLStreamPlanner.plan and that the number of solve calls equals the number of plan ids in the ledger; (iii) id-equality between the list object PDDLStreamPlanner.plan returned and the list the dispatcher iterates, with the dispatcher's loop variable logged per step so no filter, map or re-ordering can sit in between.

findings.title: G14's runtime teleport trap wraps the BulletClient instance, but execution.py and robot_utils call the pybullet module directly, so the trap would intercept nothing
findings.problem: The plan itself records that execution.py and the robot_utils motion functions address pybullet's DEFAULT client (P4.2 lines 220-221); the code confirms module-level calls with no client argument (boxel_env.py:1867 p.getBasePositionAndOrientation(obj_info.object_id); robot_utils.py:754-756 p.setJointMotorControl2/p.stepSimulation). Wrapping client.resetBasePositionAndOrientation and client.createConstraint on their BulletClient object leaves pybullet.resetBasePositionAndOrientation untouched, which is the function every main-pipeline teleport would use. The gate as worded gives a green light it has not earned.
findings.evidence: plan P4.2:220-221; boxel_env.py:1867; robot_utils.py:754-756; boxel_env.py:726-730, 745-756 (mirror writes that must be allowlisted)
findings.required_change: G14 wraps the pybullet MODULE functions (pybullet.resetBasePositionAndOrientation, pybullet.createConstraint, pybullet.resetJointState, pybullet.changeDynamics) for the episode's duration and dispatches on (physicsClientId, body id): raises for any task body on the executing client unless the caller frame is sync_to_plan_client (plan client only) or the IK save/restore on the plan-client robot (streams.py:416-418, 470-473); BulletClient forwards to the same module functions, so one wrap covers both call styles. Keep the per-collision-check pose assertion.

findings.title: B7 defers the at-home scoring rule until after watching episodes; the only mechanism that can implement a 'tolerance rule' on our side is writing DEFAULT_ARM_POS into their belief, which is CB#123
findings.plan_location: D3 (at-home asymmetry), R3, B7 ('pre-register in BF# the tolerance rule the campaign uses')
findings.problem: Their at-home atom is np.allclose(current_conf, DEFAULT_ARM_POS, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4) inside their abstract() (env.py:318-321), untouchable under H4. A conf from real joint readback either passes that test or it does not; a bridge-side 'tolerance rule' can only act by replacing the readback with a value that passes, i.e. the constant, which is exactly what belief_bridge.py:44-58 did. The plan postpones choosing that rule to B7, after two watched episodes: a scoring rule chosen from outcomes. The executor's own endpoint convergence hold stops at 2e-3 rad (robot_utils.py:780), twenty times their tolerance, so the strict test will very likely fail and the pressure to snap will be real.
findings.evidence: env.py:318-321; robot_utils.py:777-781 (settle loop exits at max joint error < 2e-3 rad); archive/tampura_bridge_v1/belief_bridge.py:44-58 (current_conf = list(DEFAULT_ARM_POS)); plan B7: 'if not, pre-register in BF# the tolerance rule the campaign uses'
findings.required_change: Decide in P4.3 D3 now, before B7: conf is ALWAYS the real readback; the headline success column uses their strict 1e-4 through their reward (G12); a second, pre-registered column 'at_home within 2e-3 rad' (the executor's own endpoint tolerance, robot_utils.py:780, cited per G9) is computed by the campaign report from the logged readback and never by writing a conf. B7 measures and reports; it does not choose. If the user wants the lenient column as the headline, that decision is recorded before B7 with its reason, and both columns are always printed.

findings.title: M2 interior regions re-spawn under every relocated cup; the rule is unstated and the obvious improvised fix is the archived per-cup bookkeeping
findings.problem: After a place, the main pipeline recasts the relocated object's fragments against the current solids and adds every new fragment to the belief as unknown (execution.py:2973-3003, 'the belief must know the fragment exists'). B5 wires interior regions 'exactly like a lateral fragment', so every relocated cup spawns a fresh unknown interior region of full cup size at its destination. Nothing in the model distinguishes it from a never-searched one; the optimistic planner can therefore choose to move the same cup again and again (equal costs, FD tie-break on grounding order), and on the 4-cup layouts the episode can burn the 900 s cap without a model-level reason. The implementer's tempting fix, 'do not cast interiors for cups already moved' or 'cups moved once are known empty', is the archived cup-name bookkeeping (boxel_policy.py:352-353, 193-205) that encoded the task structure in the wrapper. place_hiding (domain:60, 293, 314-327) was built for lateral shadows over KNOWN bodies and says nothing about this case.
findings.evidence: execution.py:2973-3003; pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl:60, 293, 314-327; archive/tampura_bridge_v1/boxel_policy.py:352-353, 193-205; plan B5: 'wired exactly like a lateral fragment'
findings.required_change: B5 states the rule before any code, as a BF# with POD wording, choosing one of: (a) an interior region cast at placement over cells that the robot observed free in its own observation record is created with status not_here and provenance 'observed free before placement' (an inference from recorded observations, logged in the ledger; G5 admits this provenance class explicitly and the gate asserts the free-cell observation precedes the placement), or (b) the region is created unknown and the resulting extra relocations are reported as the honest cost. The same rule must apply to lateral fragments of relocated objects or be justified as interior-specific; either way no per-object 'already moved' flag anywhere.

findings.title: G13's before/after hash of their tree is red by construction
findings.problem: Their rollout writes config.yml, logs/, pddl_t=*_s=*/ and a RolloutHistory pickle under save_dir, which is relative to the cwd tampura_environments (the plan's own commands cd there), and Python writes __pycache__ under both packages. A whole-tree sha256 before and after a run can never match, and a gate that is always red gets weakened silently.
findings.evidence: map_tampura facts on output artefacts (runs/run_<time>/config.yml, logs/, pddl_t=*, <datetime>.pkl); env.py:802 (problems path relative to cwd); plan P4.6 COMMANDS (cd /root/tampura-work/tampura_environments)
findings.required_change: Hash the source set only (*.py, env_configs/*.yml, problems/*.json, models/) and name the excluded paths (runs/, logs/, __pycache__) in the gate's docstring; additionally assert the loaded module __file__ for every tampura module is under the hashed tree.

findings.title: G3's 'executed sequence == planned sequence' is wrong for a replanning loop and will be relaxed ad hoc
findings.problem: The main loop abandons the current plan after every sense outcome that changes the belief and on executor failures; the executed sequence is a PREFIX of each plan, followed by a new plan id. Stated as equality, the gate fails on every honest episode and whoever relaxes it may also admit insertions.
findings.evidence: execution.py:2445-2449 (sense branches 'break to replan'); test_full_pipeline.py:1515-1549 (move executed through a runtime plan_motion re-solve to the planned q2)
findings.required_change: G3: for each plan id, the executed primitives are a prefix of that plan in order with identical args; every truncation is attributed to a logged sense outcome or executor status; zero executed primitives lack a (plan id, step index); the runtime plan_motion re-solve is logged per move with q2 equal to the planned config.

findings.title: B1(b) already derives a die class size from the scene files' z values, which G9 forbids
findings.problem: The plan writes 'die (expected ~2.2 cm from the scene z, YCB 062 says 1.6 cm; measure)'. The 2.2 cm comes from problems/*.json instance poses, not from the mesh. Even as an expectation it is an instance read feeding a class constant, and NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS drives boxel_fits for every pre-sense target (streams.py:530-549).
findings.evidence: plan B1(b); streams.py:530-549; map_tampura fact on problems/*.json z values (0.0493, 0.0523, 0.0209)
findings.required_change: B1(b) derives every class size from the mesh files alone (trimesh extents of textured.obj / textured_vhacd.obj per category) and the record strikes the scene-z expectation; G9's check lists problems/*.json among the forbidden sources for any constant.

findings.title: Where the initial observation and boxelization run relative to their clock is left ambiguous
findings.problem: D2 and G18 say all of our planning and execution happen inside env.step; B2's deliverable builds OBJECT and interior boxels in the driver before rollout. TAMPURA's own initial image and visibility build also run outside their clock in env.initialize (env.py:853-869) while their stream sampling runs inside, so either placement is defensible, but an unstated split invites a later convenient choice.
findings.evidence: env.py:853-869; policy.py:104-136 (clock starts at rollout, time_deltas at history.add); plan B2 deliverable vs D2
findings.required_change: State in D2 that env_adapter construction and the initial observation run inside execute_fn (so time_deltas covers them), or that they mirror env.initialize's exclusion exactly; in both cases log their duration as a separate ledger field reported in the table notes.

what_the_plan_gets_right: D2/D3 is the option the forensic read sanctioned: their rollout, Belief.update, abstract() and get_reward run untouched (spec.py:336-338 dispatches by name; verify() accepts an input-less schema, spec.py:240-264), and the reward inputs come from one audited adapter fed by physical readback instead of belief_bridge's writes.

G12 scores both arms from RolloutHistory.rewards[-1] and bans the bridge-side RESULT line; the exact seed set, the pinned seed-to-scene map and the stratification by layout are correct given random.choice(os.listdir) (env.py:801-811).

D4 rejects an external camera (the archived _cam_check probing) and D5 rejects lift-and-look and sense-while-holding; M1 turns the archived unplanned park into a planned move that the planner pays for.

M2 is a geometric belief region wired through blocks_view_at/view_clear and sensed over a grid, not a per-cup flag; boxel_fits already uses the NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS class prior (streams.py:530-549), and the plan twin parks boxel-less bodies at _PLAN_CLIENT_PARK (boxel_env.py:751-753), so the RRT cannot see the die.

G4, G5 and G6 as specified would catch the three decisive archived violations: _next_place_xy (boxel_policy.py:160-176, executed xy != planned boxel centre), known_empty_shadows=all_shadows (boxel_policy.py:253-258, no mark_sensed event in the ledger) and the unconditional mark_at_home after execute_go_home (boxel_policy.py:372-381, the no_path fault test).

D9 and P4.6 pre-register budgets, repetitions, interleaving, Wilson intervals and the no-action-cap decision; R7 forbids new retry policies outside the main pipeline; D7/G9 forbid per-seed constants; the runtime plan_motion re-solve before a move is disclosed as main-pipeline behaviour (test_full_pipeline.py:1515-1549).
D8 refuses the archived friction raise and makes the static-to-dynamic conversion a build-time, all-bodies, disclosed fact rather than a pick-time patch.
